title: Video game sales that level off

stimulus.title: Total sales of a video game
stimulus.html:
A video game studio tracks the total number of copies of a new game sold since its release. The table gives the total sales SS, in thousands of copies, tt weeks after release. The total sales are modeled by the function S(t)=a+bln⁡tS(t) = a + b\ln t, whose graph passes through both data points.
Total sales S, in thousands of copies, t weeks after release
tt (weeks)18
SS (thousands of copies)1237

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Use the given data to write two equations that can be used to find the values of the constants aa and bb in the expression for S(t)S(t).

rubric.point: Two correct equations, one for each data point
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a + b\ln 1 = 12</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>37</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a + b\ln 8 = 37</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a + b\ln 1 = 12</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>37</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a + b\ln 8 = 37</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Find the values of aa and bb as decimal approximations.
parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln 1 = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = 12</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b\ln 8 = 25</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>25</mn><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mn>12.022</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = \frac{25}{\ln 8} \approx 12.022</annotation></semantics></math> (stored, not rounded, for later parts).

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Use the given data to find the average rate of change of SS, in thousands of copies per week, from t=1t = 1 to t=8t = 8. Express your answer as a decimal approximation. Show the computations that lead to your answer.

rubric.point: The difference quotient from the data, about <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3.571</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3.571</annotation></semantics></math> thousand copies per week

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{S(8) - S(1)}{8 - 1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>37</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><mn>7</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{37 - 12}{7}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>25</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{25}{7}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>3.571</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 3.571</annotation></semantics></math> thousand copies per week, the slope of the secant line through <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 12)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>37</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(8, 37)</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Use the average rate of change from part B(i) to estimate the total sales at t=4t = 4. Is this estimate an overestimate or an underestimate of the value of the model S(4)S(4)? Explain your reasoning using the concavity of the graph of SS.

rubric.point: The estimate <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>25</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac><mo>≈</mo><mn>22.714</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12 + 3 \cdot \frac{25}{7} \approx 22.714</annotation></semantics></math> on the secant line, and "underestimate" because <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> is concave down on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 8]</annotation></semantics></math>, so its graph lies above the secant line
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>≈</mo><mn>22.714</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 22.714</annotation></semantics></math>; underestimate, since <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b > 0</annotation></semantics></math> makes <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> concave down on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 8]</annotation></semantics></math> and the secant line lies below the graph

the rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> is decreasing on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 8]</annotation></semantics></math>, so the secant lies below the graph there

parts.sample: Using the secant line through <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1, 12)</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>25</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12 + \frac{25}{7}(4 - 1)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">≈</mo><mn>22.714</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 22.714</annotation></semantics></math> thousand copies. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(t) = 12 + b\ln t</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b > 0</annotation></semantics></math> is concave down on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1, 8]</annotation></semantics></math>, so the graph of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> lies above the secant line on that interval and the estimate is an underestimate. (Indeed <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>≈</mo><mn>28.667</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(4) \approx 28.667</annotation></semantics></math>.)

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: According to the model, when will the total sales reach <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>60</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60</annotation></semantics></math> thousand copies? Give your answer correct to three decimal places.

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>54.192</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t \approx 54.192</annotation></semantics></math> weeks, from solving <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(t) = 60</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: Solve <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>60</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12 + b\ln t = 60</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>48</mn><mi>b</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln t = \frac{48}{b}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>48</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msup><mo>≈</mo><mn>54.192</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = e^{48/b} \approx 54.192</annotation></semantics></math> weeks.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: The studio expects sales of the game to level off after a few months, as most interested players have bought it. Explain why the model's error is likely to grow for values of tt greater than 88, and what that means for the answer to part C(i).

rubric.point: The data stop at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 8</annotation></semantics></math>, so the model is unsupported after that; the model keeps increasing without bound while actual sales level off, so the model overestimates more and more, and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>60</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60</annotation></semantics></math> thousand may come later or never
accept: The model is fit to data only up to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> weeks; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{t \to \infty} S(t) = \infty</annotation></semantics></math> but real sales level off, so the gap between model and actual sales grows and the predicted time of about <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>54</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54</annotation></semantics></math> weeks is too early

parts.sample: The model was built from data with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 \le t \le 8</annotation></semantics></math>, so past week <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> no data support it. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S(t)</annotation></semantics></math> keeps increasing without bound, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">lim</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow></munder><mi>S</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lim_{t \to \infty} S(t) = \infty</annotation></semantics></math>, while actual sales level off. So the model's predictions get further above the actual sales as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> increases, and the time of about 54.2 weeks from part C(i) is likely too early: actual sales may reach <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>60</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60</annotation></semantics></math> thousand much later, or not at all.
